subject: Archaeology
title: Genetic Ethics: Who Owns Ancient DNA?
description: A micro-lesson that makes Genetic Ethics: Who Owns Ancient DNA? usable.

hook.text: DNA labs process hundreds of skeletons yearly. Some communities ask: who gave permission?

buildup.text: Some studies were published without consulting descendants. Bones were destroyed.

discovery.text: In 2021, geneticists published ethics guidelines calling for community consent.

twist.text: Some results are sensitive. Genetic findings can challenge national origin stories.

climax.text: The best projects co-design research with communities and share results before publishing.

punchline.text: Science can read anyone's ancestor. Ethics asks whether it should.

quiz.question: What ethical issue emerged in ancient DNA research?
options: DNA studies are too expensive for universities
Bones were sampled without consulting descendant communities
Ancient DNA results are too unreliable for journals
